extracted.intended_audience: museum organizations preparing an IMLS Museums for America (MFA) FY2025 grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a complete Museums for America (MFA) FY2025 grant application to IMLS, following program goals, eligibility, document, budget, performance measurement, and digital/conservation guidance in the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Organization type
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible, the organization must be (1) a unit of State, local, or Tribal government; or (2) a private, nonprofit organization with tax-exempt status under the Internal Revenue Code (proof required if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide proof of nonprofit status where applicable. Native American Tribal organizations may apply if they otherwise meet eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Organization location
rubrics_metrics.description: Your organization must be located in one of the 50 States, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, or the Republic of Palau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Museum definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A museum must: use a professional staff; be organized on a permanent basis for educational, cultural heritage, or aesthetic purposes; own or use tangible objects (including living collections); care for these objects; and exhibit these objects to the general public on a regular basis through facilities it owns or operates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of institutions that qualify (if they meet requirements) include anthropology museums, aquariums, arboretums, art museums, botanical gardens, children’s/youth museums, historic houses/sites, natural history museums, planetariums, science/technology centers, specialized museums, and zoological parks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: 'Professional staff' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution uses a professional staff if it employs at least one staff member, or the full-time equivalent, whether paid or unpaid, primarily engaged in acquisition, care, or exhibition to the public of objects owned or used by the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: 'Exhibit to the general public' threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution that exhibits objects to the general public for at least 120 days a year is deemed to exhibit objects on a regular basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions that do not meet the 120-day threshold or for which exhibition is not a primary purpose may still be eligible under certain circumstances per 2 C.F.R. § 3187.3; see regulation for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Museum located within a parent organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A museum within a parent organization may apply on its own behalf only if it can independently fulfill all eligibility requirements, functions as a discrete unit, has its own fully segregated and itemized operating budget, and has authority to make the application on its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of those three conditions cannot be met, the museum must apply through its parent organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Nonprofit affiliated organization applying on behalf of a museum
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprofit organization affiliated with a museum may be eligible if its sole mission is to support the specified museum; it has the ability to administer the project; and it can ensure compliance with the NOFO and applicable law (including IMLS Assurances and Certifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide an agreement from the museum that details activities performed by applicant and museum and binds the museum to the statements and assurances in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application limits and ineligible submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for renewal or supplementation of currently active IMLS awards are not eligible to compete with new award applications. If eligible, an applicant may submit multiple applications for separate and distinct projects. Applications from ineligible applicants will not be reviewed or awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must be complete and adhere to program guidelines and funding restrictions; missing required documents may result in rejection (see 2 C.F.R. § 3187.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and collaborations: lead applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more institutions work together, one must meet all eligibility requirements, serve as the lead applicant, and administer the award on behalf of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If funded, the lead applicant will be programmatically, fiscally, and legally responsible for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding range and application rejection for out-of-range requests
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS may reject applications if the federal funding requested (including direct and indirect costs) is less than $5,000 or more than $250,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure the requested amount falls within $5,000–$250,000 to avoid rejection for this reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share requirement (eligibility criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must provide non-federal funds equal to or greater than the amount of the federal award (1:1 cost share). Cost share is an eligibility criterion and is not considered in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost share examples include cash outlays, contributions of property and services, and in-kind contributions (e.g., staff or volunteer time). Applicants must include at least 1:1 cost share on the IMLS Budget Form or risk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program alignment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must align their project with one of three MFA program goals (Lifelong Learning; Community Engagement; Collections Stewardship and Access) and one associated objective, and clearly identify these choices in the Narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS expects each award to contribute meaningfully to program and agency-level goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measures and Performance Measurement Plan (PMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS uses four performance measures—Effectiveness, Efficiency, Quality, and Timeliness—to assess projects. Applicants must provide a Performance Measurement Plan describing how they will use these four measures to monitor and assess project performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance Measurement Plan has a recommended page limit of 2 pages. See NOFO for definitions and examples of each measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and unallowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS funds and cost share may be used only for allowable costs per IMLS and OMB cost-principle rules (2 C.F.R. part 200 and 2 C.F.R. part 3187). Examples of generally allowable costs include personnel salaries and fringe, travel for key staff/consultants, materials and equipment related to project activities, accessibility technologies, participant support costs (if documented), collections storage/exhibit equipment, third-party costs, design/publication, program evaluation, training, paid internships/fellowships, stipends/honoraria, and indirect/overhead costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable costs include general fundraising, endowment contributions, general operating support, acquisition of collections, general advertising/public relations solely promotional (not related to the specific project), construction/renovation (generally not allowable), social activities/receptions/entertainment, and research projects. Contact IMLS with questions about specific items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party costs and subrecipient vs contractor determination
rubrics_metrics.description: When paying third parties (partners, consultants, vendors, etc.), applicants are responsible for determining whether each third party is a subrecipient or contractor and including that determination in agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS grant funds generally may not be provided to other U.S. government agencies. See 2 C.F.R. § 200.331 for guidance on subrecipient and contractor determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost options and rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may: use a negotiated indirect cost rate not to exceed their current NICRA; use a proposed rate pending negotiation (must be finalized by award time); use a de minimis rate not to exceed 15% of MTDC if they do not have a NICRA and are not subject to other requirements; or not include indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include indirect cost rate and base in the Budget Justification if indirect costs are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizing statute, regulations, and Uniform Guidance applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients must follow IMLS regulations (2 C.F.R. part 3187), the authorizing statute (20 U.S.C. § 9101 et seq., especially § 9173), and applicable OMB Uniform Guidance (2 C.F.R. part 200). For awards made after Oct 1, 2024, the Uniform Guidance Revisions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFO attempts alignment with revisions; in event of differences, the revisions govern for awards after Oct 1, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity and nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, or age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Civil Rights Officer for further information; include nondiscrimination compliance as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required registrations before applying
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying, organizations must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), an active SAM.gov registration, and an active Grants.gov registration with an approved Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register early—SAM.gov can take several weeks; Grants.gov registration can take several days. Consult Guidance for Required Registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission method and identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted electronically through Grants.gov Workspace or a Grants.gov system-to-system solution. Use Funding Opportunity Number MFA-FY25 or Assistance Listing Number 45.301 to locate the application package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS may provide audio or paper copies upon request for accessibility; TTY users information provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application components, required documents, and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must include required components: SF-424S; IMLS Museum Program Information Form; Organizational Profile (recommended 1 page); Strategic Plan Summary (recommended 2 pages); Narrative (PDF, 7 pages max); Schedule of Completion (1 page per year recommended); IMLS Budget Form (PDF); Budget Justification (PDF); List of Key Project Staff and Consultants (1 page recommended); Resumes (PDF, 2 pages each recommended); Performance Measurement Plan (PDF, 2 pages recommended); and any other listed required forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required or conditionally required documents are missing, the application may be considered incomplete and rejected. Follow exact file names and formats listed in NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionally required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must include certain documents if applicable: Proof of Private Nonprofit Status; Final Federally Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA); Digital Products Plan (2 pages recommended); Detailed Condition Reports and/or Conservation Treatment Proposals; and other conditionally required items identified in the NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Conditionally Required Documents section to determine applicability and required supporting documentation (e.g., museum agreement when a nonprofit applies on behalf of a museum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format, file naming, file size, and attachment sequencing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Aside from SF-424S and IMLS Program Information Form, all components must be submitted as PDFs. Use standard formatting and fonts. Limit individual file sizes to 200 MB or less. Use the specified naming conventions and only permitted characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, hyphen, space, period). Attach components in the sequence listed in the attachment table; use the 'Other Attachments Form' if more than 15 attachments and adhere to its ordering requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file names use disallowed characters, Grants.gov may reject the application. Follow attachment ordering rules carefully to avoid submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS will remove any pages that exceed stated page limits and will not send them to reviewers as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to page limits for each component; extra pages are discarded before review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Profile content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational Profile (recommended 1 page) should include the organization's mission/statement of purpose (source and approval date), governance structure (and relationship to parent organization if applicable), service area (communities/audiences served with demographics and geography), and a brief history focusing on the unit carrying out the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save as OrganizationalProfile.pdf; recommended one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Plan Summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary (recommended 2 pages) of the organization's strategic plan to contextualize the project and link it to institutional goals; indicate who approved the plan and when. Do not submit the entire strategic plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save as StrategicPlan.pdf; limit to recommended length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative component must be submitted as PDF and is limited to 7 pages maximum. The Narrative should clearly describe the project, its relation to the selected program goal/objective, expected results, and measurable outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS uses the Narrative to evaluate alignment with program goals; follow NOFO guidance on content and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan requirements (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants creating or collecting digital products must submit a Digital Products Plan (recommended 2 pages) describing Type, Availability, Access, and Sustainability of digital products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS staff and peer reviewers will assess the plan and it will be important in funding decisions. Follow FADGI and other standards as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the digital content, resources, or assets to be created or collected, including quantities, digital file formats, accompanying metadata, and relevant standards. For software, specify programming languages, platforms, frameworks, and explain choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include still images, audio, moving images, object inventories, metadata schemas, documentation, and software source code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how digital products will be made openly available (as appropriate), delivery strategy (openly online, access-controlled, kiosks, recorded programs), underlying hardware/software platforms, and explain any limitations in the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS encourages open access and expects publications produced under an award to be made publicly accessible without charge. Indicate delivery platforms (e.g., repositories, IIIF-enabled delivery) and any access restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Access, rights, and sensitivities
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify licenses under which digital products will be shared (e.g., Creative Commons), describe intellectual property rights asserted and any limitations, and explain how privacy concerns or cultural sensitivities will be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS allows award recipients to copyright work developed under an award but reserves a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right for federal government purposes. IMLS encourages releasing files under open-source licenses to maximize access and reuse; work products should be distributed for free or at cost unless IMLS approves otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plans for preserving and maintaining digital products during and after the period of performance, identify appropriate retention periods for different digital products, and address storage systems, shared repositories, technical documentation, migration planning, and committed organizational funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between long-lived outputs requiring permanent preservation and short/medium-term outputs (drafts, preliminary analyses, social media).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Conservation Surveys — General
rubrics_metrics.description: General conservation surveys should broadly assess an organization's collections and environmental conditions, describe conditions, identify conservation problems, and suggest future conservation activities in general terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General conservation survey report should include an executive summary; general information about the museum; survey goals; overview of collections, condition, and care policies; descriptions of building/facilities/exhibit/storage areas; climate control and environmental conditions; staffing information including training needs; and prioritized recommendations for future conservation care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Conservation Surveys — Detailed conservation survey
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed conservation survey is an item-by-item examination of all or part of a collection by a conservation professional producing condition reports identifying condition, treatment priority, and cost/method of treatment. A detailed survey should precede any request to fund treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed survey to establish treatment priorities and resource/time needs; include condition reports as supporting documentation when requesting conservation treatment funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Conservation Surveys — Environmental survey
rubrics_metrics.description: An environmental survey assesses environmental conditions (temperature, relative humidity, light) conducted by a conservation professional with other consultants as needed, and can be used to identify problems, set priorities, design solutions, develop monitoring programs, and map collections (for living plants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental surveys may be funded to survey conditions in exhibition and storage areas and other collections housing locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification instructions (sections and required detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget Justification must follow the IMLS Budget Form headings and address both grant funds and cost share. Sections include: (1) Salaries and Wages — identify each person paid, role, base salary, percentage/time allocated, and cost computation; (2) Fringe Benefits — identify rates and bases; (3) Travel — purpose, traveler name, origin/destination, and cost breakdown; (4) Supplies, Materials, and Equipment — list items, number, unit cost, and vendor quotes; (5) Subawards and Contracts — identify each third party, role, activities, cost, and designation as subrecipient or contractor; (6) Student Support — explain calculation method; (7) Other Costs; (8) Total Direct Costs — specify amounts requested and cost share; (9) Indirect Costs — identify rate and base; (10) Total Project Costs — indicate totals and cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate detail and supporting documents (e.g., vendor quotes) to justify costs. For new staff, explain alignment of estimated salary with local standards. Be explicit about volunteer cost share valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumes and staff documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: List of Key Project Staff and Consultants (recommended 1 page) and Resumes for key staff/consultants (PDF, 2 pages each recommended) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include names, roles, and brief qualifications; follow file naming conventions (Projectstaff.pdf, Resumes.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and deadline enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via Grants.gov by 11:59 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time on November 15, 2024. Late submissions will not be considered. Applications missing required or conditionally required documents may be considered incomplete and rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start registrations early and use the NOFO readiness checklist to ensure completeness; emergency extensions policy is described in the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project start date and period of performance constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated start date for new awards is September 1, 2025. Anticipated period of performance is September 1, 2025 – August 31, 2028; project activities may be carried out for one to three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project schedule and Schedule of Completion accordingly (Schedule of Completion recommended 1 page per year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords selection for Program Information Form
rubrics_metrics.description: In Section 8 of the IMLS Museum Program Information Form, applicants must select 1–8 keywords that best characterize the project from an IMLS-provided alphabetical list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS may use these keywords in reporting and as tools for applicants and the public to find relevant awards. Choose keywords that accurately reflect project content and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital products licensing and government use rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients may copyright works developed under an award, but IMLS reserves for Federal Government purposes a royalty-free, nonexclusive, and irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use the work and authorize others to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS expects recipients to release digital files under open-source licenses where possible and to distribute work products for free or at cost unless IMLS approves another arrangement in writing.
